questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a research note, what is the configuration of a chiral center whose lowest-priority group points away and whose 1-to-2-to-3 order runs clockwise?

options.text: S, with the lowest group pointing away
options.misconception: reverses the clockwise convention

options.text: R, with the lowest group pointing away
The center is achiral and has no descriptor
options.misconception: mistakes four different groups for a mirror plane

options.text: E, because groups straddle a double bond
options.misconception: confuses R/S with alkene E/Z notation

questions.explanation: With the lowest-priority group directed away, a clockwise 1-2-3 sequence is assigned R; viewing from the opposite side would invert the descriptor.
questions.hint: Point the lowest group away, then read one to two to three.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.learningObjective: Identify the most stable chair conformation
questions.stem: A student is asked: which conformation places a bulky tert-butyl group in an equatorial position?

options.misconception: boats are higher in energy than chairs
overlooks severe 1,3-diaxial strain
doubly destabilizes the conformation

questions.explanation: A chair places substituents in equatorial sites where 1,3-diaxial interactions are avoided, and a tert-butyl group has a very strong equatorial preference.
questions.hint: Bulky groups prefer equatorial sites in a chair.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.learningObjective: Rank acids by conjugate base stability
questions.stem: For the structure at hand, which feature most strongly stabilizes a conjugate base and raises the acidity of its parent acid?

options.text: A longer alkyl chain at the acidic site
options.misconception: alkyl groups destabilize anions by induction

options.text: A greater number of alkyl substituents
options.misconception: electron donation raises the pKa

options.text: More steric bulk around the acidic proton
options.misconception: sterics do not stabilize the anion

options.text: Resonance delocalization of the negative charge

questions.explanation: Acidity rises when the conjugate base is stabilized, most effectively by resonance or electron-withdrawing induction, both of which lower the pKa.
questions.hint: Think about what stabilizes the anion formed.

provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.learningObjective: Classify a reagent by electronic role
questions.stem: For the case in question, what role does a species bearing a lone pair and a negative charge usually play in a polar reaction?

options.misconception: confuses electron donors with acceptors
a lone-pair donor is a Lewis base
ignores the drive to neutralize charge

questions.explanation: A negatively charged species with available electrons donates them to an electron-poor center, which is exactly the definition of a nucleophile.
questions.hint: Electron-rich species seek electron-poor partners.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In class discussion, which statement about two valid resonance contributors of a carboxylate ion is correct?

options.misconception: resonance is not a time-dependent equilibrium

options.text: They differ only in electron placement, not atom positions

options.misconception: resonance never moves atoms

options.text: The less stable contributor does not exist at all
options.misconception: all valid contributors shape the hybrid

questions.explanation: Resonance contributors are alternative Lewis structures with identical atom connectivity; only electrons move, and the real species is a weighted hybrid of them.
questions.hint: Resonance moves electrons, never nuclei.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Working through the mechanism, which condition must a planar, cyclic, fully conjugated ring meet to be aromatic?

options.text: It must contain exactly 4n pi electrons
options.misconception: planar 4n systems are antiaromatic

options.text: It must contain an odd number of pi electrons
options.misconception: an odd count leaves an unpaired electron

options.text: It must contain 4n plus 2 pi electrons
It must be fused to a second ring
options.misconception: a single ring can be aromatic

questions.explanation: Aromaticity requires a planar, cyclic, fully conjugated ring holding 4n+2 pi electrons; a planar 4n system is instead antiaromatic and destabilized.
questions.hint: Recall the 4n+2 rule of Huckel.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Given the transformation, decide: which functional group contains a carbonyl carbon bonded to an OR group?

options.misconception: a ketone has two carbon groups on the carbonyl
an aldehyde bears a hydrogen on the carbonyl
an acid bears an OH on the carbonyl

questions.explanation: An ester has the motif R-C(=O)-OR with an alkoxy group replacing the acid OH; ketones and aldehydes instead carry carbon or hydrogen substituents on the carbonyl.
questions.hint: Look for a carbonyl bonded to an oxygen.

questions.stem: A written test asks: in an SN1 reaction of a tertiary halide, which step is rate determining?

no deprotonation is needed here
SN1 is unimolecular in the slow step

questions.explanation: The slow step of an SN1 reaction is ionization, where the leaving group departs to give a carbocation; nucleophilic capture of that cation then occurs quickly.

questions.stem: A chemist observes the following: which factor best explains why an alcohol boils higher than an ether of similar molar mass?

options.text: E, because groups straddle a double bond

doubly destabilizes the conformation

a lone-pair donor is a Lewis base
ignores the drive to neutralize charge

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: You are given the following: which condition must a planar, cyclic, fully conjugated ring meet to be aromatic?

options.text: It must contain exactly 4n pi electrons

options.text: It must contain an odd number of pi electrons
options.misconception: an odd count leaves an unpaired electron

options.text: It must contain 4n plus 2 pi electrons

questions.explanation: Subtracting the two values, 16 minus 4.8 is about 11.2, so acetic acid is stronger by roughly eleven pKa units, corresponding to about eleven orders of magnitude in Ka.
questions.hint: Subtract the smaller pKa from the larger.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.learningObjective: Count pi electrons in an aromatic ion
questions.stem: For the measurement, the cyclopentadienyl anion has four pi electrons from its two double bonds plus one lone pair. How many pi electrons does it contain in total?
questions.explanation: Two double bonds contribute four pi electrons and the lone pair on the anionic carbon contributes two more, giving six, which satisfies the 4n+2 rule with n equal to one.
questions.hint: Add the lone pair to the double-bond electrons.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: For the measurement, how many stereocenters are present in 2,3-dibromobutane?
questions.explanation: Each of carbons 2 and 3 bears bromine, hydrogen, a methyl group and a different carbon chain, so both carbons are stereocenters, giving two in total.
questions.hint: Examine each carbon bearing four different groups.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: For the measurement, a hydrocarbon has molecular formula C6H10. What is its degree of unsaturation?
questions.explanation: Degree of unsaturation equals (2C+2-H)/2, which for C6H10 is (12+2-10)/2 = 2, indicating two rings or pi bonds in the structure.
questions.hint: Apply the formula (2C+2-H)/2.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: For the measurement, in the most stable chair of butane viewed along the central bond, how many gauche interactions does the anti conformer have?
questions.explanation: The anti conformer places the two methyl groups 180 degrees apart, so there are no gauche methyl-methyl interactions; the gauche conformers each have one.
questions.hint: Anti conformation has zero methyl gauche contacts.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: For the measurement, how many pi electrons are delocalized over the ring of benzene?
questions.explanation: Benzene has three conjugated double bonds, each contributing two pi electrons, so six electrons are delocalized around the ring, matching the 4n+2 rule with n equal to one.
questions.hint: Three double bonds give six pi electrons.
